Logistic regression has the lowest log loss on these 48 test rows:

CV choice: Logistic regression

?How the default model was chosen

Logistic regression was selected using 5-fold cross-validation on the
training rows. 15 settings were tried; one fitted representative per
successful family is kept here.Score definitions

?Score definitions

log loss: Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers;
lower is better. Brier score: Mean squared error of the positive-class
probability, from 0 (best) to 1 (worst); lower is better. binned
calibration gap: Average absolute gap between grouped probabilities and
observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value depends on the
evaluation sample and grouping. accuracy: Share of evaluation rows
assigned to the correct class; higher is better. balanced accuracy:
Average recall across the positive and negative classes; higher is
better. Unavailable when either class is absent from the evaluation
rows. ROC AUC: Chance that a random positive receives a higher score
than a random negative; higher is better.

How costs were measured

Times are measured on this machine. Fit time covers the retained fit,
not the entire cross-validation search; prediction time covers this
evaluation batch. A displayed ~0 means no elapsed time was recorded;
timer resolution varies by platform. It does not mean the operation
takes no time. Size is an approximate R object measurement, not a count
of learned rules. These measurements are not hardware-independent
benchmarks.

Training selection, settings and failures

Automatic tuning

## How was the primary model selected?

AutoXplainR divided only the training portion into 5 folds. Each
configuration repeatedly fitted on some training folds and scored on the
remaining fold. Preprocessing was learned again inside every fold. The
outer test set shown in the evaluation section did not participate in
this choice.

**Actual final configuration:** `linear_01`. This is the configuration
behind the primary fitted model.

### Selection rule

one-standard-error (prefer the documented family priority, then the
least-flexible near-best setting within that family). The default
one-standard-error rule first uses the configured family priority, then
prefers the least-flexible eligible setting inside that family. Use the
best-score rule when predictive score alone should decide.

Values: Configuration, Model family, Settings

**Within-family flexibility proxy:** each family uses the definition
recorded in `tuning_results(result)$learner_manifest`. Those values
order settings only inside the same family; their units are not
comparable across linear, additive, tree, ensemble, kernel, neighbor, or
neural models.

**Do not quote the resampled tuning score as final performance.** It
guided model selection. The test result above estimates performance on
rows kept outside model fitting and selection.

Configuration ranking used only resamples of the outer training rows;
the held-out evaluation rows were untouched until final scoring. Folds
were assigned automatically within the outer training data. Every
outer-training row received an out-of-fold prediction.

### How are these model families different?

**Prior/model-capacity knowledge:** the nonlinearity and interaction
columns describe each model family. They say what each family can
represent; they do not show that this fitted model actually used those
patterns.

| Model | Family | Backend | Capacity: nonlinearity | Capacity: interactions | Computed log loss |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| resampling-selected logistic regression | linear | stats | none unless encoded in features | none unless specified in features | 0.492 |
| tuned neural network alternative | neural | nnet | smooth and flexible | automatic through hidden units | 0.5274 |
| tuned decision tree alternative | tree | rpart | stepwise | automatic along tree paths | 0.5844 |

Values: Model, Family, Backend

**Computed evidence from this analysis:** evaluation performance and
paired prediction disagreement are calculated on common evaluation rows.
Repeated permutation feature importance in the Patterns section is also
computed evidence of model reliance, not a property guaranteed by the
family card.

- resampling-selected logistic regression has the best supplied log_loss
  score (0.492).
- tuned neural network alternative and tuned decision tree alternative
  differ most on average (0.187 using absolute difference in
  positive-class probability).

## Feature importance & effects?Exploring fitted effectsALE follows local changes in predictions and centers the effect at zero. These describe fitted associations, not the consequences of an intervention.

## Checks requiring attention

### The shuffle interval for \`neural_model\` / \`months\` does not resolve the sign of the mean loss change.

Affected evidence: [tuned neural network alternative /
months](#evidence-6e657572616c5f6d6f64656c-6d6f6e746873)

The fixed-sample Monte Carlo interval includes zero.

**Next:** Inspect the repeat distribution; more shuffles address Monte
Carlo error only.

Diagnostic coverage and association evidence

**evaluation: computed.** Ordered observations, outcomes and event
semantics agree; independence and representativeness are not established
by these checks.

**association: computed.** Limited pairwise screen: absolute Spearman
correlation for numeric pairs, correlation ratio for mixed pairs, and
Cramer's V for categorical pairs. Small values do not establish
independence or exclude nonlinear or joint dependence.

**permutation: computed.** Loss changes describe these shuffles. The
intervals quantify shuffle randomness, not sampling, fitting or
selection uncertainty.

**comparison: insufficient evidence.** Fewer than two supplied models
meet the performance tolerance.

**resources: computed.**

**model_behavior: computed.**

**prediction_disagreement: computed.**

**decision_cutoffs: computed.**

## Evaluation-sample uncertainty

**Paired bootstrap: not run.** No evaluation-sample interval was
requested.

Compute intervals in R

    render_model_report(result, "report.html", uncertainty = TRUE)

The bootstrap requires supported independent sampling units; time-based
evaluation needs a different design.

### What changes when the decision cutoff moves?

The model reports the probability of **yes**. Calling that class at 0.5
is a convention. A lower cutoff usually catches more positives and
creates more false positives; a higher cutoff usually does the reverse.

| Cutoff | Predicted positive | Sensitivity | Specificity | Precision | Accuracy | False positives | False negatives |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| 0.30 | 35.4% | 53.8% | 71.4% | 41.2% | 66.7% | 10.00 | 6.00 |
| 0.50 | 16.7% | 38.5% | 91.4% | 62.5% | 77.1% | 3.00 | 8.00 |
| 0.70 | 6.2% | 23.1% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 79.2% | 0.00 | 10.00 |

Values: Cutoff, Predicted positive, Sensitivity

**No cutoff is recommended here.** The relative consequences of false
positives and false negatives belong to the application. If a cutoff is
chosen using these evaluation rows, evaluate it again on different
representative data.

No missing input values were observed in training or evaluation.

considered for a split; minbucket is the minimum rows in a leaf. cp sets
a minimum relative improvement for splitting. The fitted depth and leaf
count above describe the resulting tree.

Metric definitions

Definitions for every metric

- log loss: Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers;
  lower is better.
- Brier score: Mean squared error of the positive-class probability,
  from 0 (best) to 1 (worst); lower is better.
- binned calibration gap: Average absolute gap between grouped
  probabilities and observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value
  depends on the evaluation sample and grouping.
- accuracy: Share of evaluation rows assigned to the correct class;
  higher is better.
- balanced accuracy: Average recall across the positive and negative
  classes; higher is better. Unavailable when either class is absent
  from the evaluation rows.
- ROC AUC: Chance that a random positive receives a higher score than a
  random negative; higher is better.

### Reading this analysis

Scores describe the recorded evaluation split. Feature effects describe
fitted associations. Use independent evaluation data for a final
assessment after changing models or predictors. Neither this report nor
a passing diagnostic establishes causal effects.
